Its reading lists two directive items, one citing another job, plus one plain exclusion. Exactly 2 steward-channel requests result. Each text holds the job id and the `Out-of-scope item number: <job> ` line, and has non-empty request_text_acceptance and request_text_touches. dependency_ids_in and followed_up_ids are empty and retried_job is None. The text comes from RequestQueue::apply, which calls StewardRequest::from_change and then StewardRequest::new (steward.rs:635, 669).

criteria.evidence: I ran it: 2 passed. The close test lands one job with the file-list exclusion and one with an empty list. Neither adds a steward request, and the records hold only the job itself.

criteria.criterion: `cargo test` shows queuing is idempotent: closing, retrying or resuming the same job twice yields each follow-up request once, and the number queued per job is capped.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: 4 passed. (1) Pure test: re-queuing with the existing texts, or with reworded items, gives already_queued and no files; a reading of 7 items queues 5 and skips 2; a duplicate item queues once. (2) Calling follow_up_files again on a closed job gives nothing and logs 'already queued'. (3) A failed job and its 'try again on' retry with reworded items: 3 requests in total, all keyed to the first job, none to the retry. (4) A job held on low disk queues nothing; after athena.retry and go it lands with 3 requests keyed to the held job.

findings.summary: Scope: the hook lives in run/close.rs, which is not on the expected-deliverables list. Listed manage.rs, steward.rs and reading.rs are unchanged.
findings.evidence: git diff --stat shows close.rs changed and no change to manage.rs, steward.rs or reading.rs. The reading said manage.rs was where a job closes 'which the producer must confirm', and the accepted plan named close.rs. close_dispatched is the single close path for dispatched jobs (run/mod.rs:1328, 1349, 1355, 1376), so the placement is right and nothing beyond the request was added.

findings.summary: Soundness: once any follow-up exists for a retry chain, later jobs in that chain queue nothing at all, even a new follow-up.
findings.evidence: chain_has_marker returns already_queued for the whole chain. The CHANGELOG states this cost ('a retry that names a new follow-up queues none of it, so queue that one by hand'). A per-item check (for example, matching normalised item text against existing Item: lines, alongside the chain marker for reworded duplicates) would avoid dropping genuinely new follow-ups. The current rule deliberately trades that for robustness against rewording, which criterion 3 requires.

findings.summary: Soundness: the rule that 'propose' within three words of 'job' or 'request' counts as a follow-up can match a plain exclusion.
findings.evidence: PROPOSED_NOUNS includes 'job' and 'request' with PROPOSE_REACH = 3, so an exclusion like 'We do not propose a new job state' would queue a request. The cap of 5 and the once-per-chain marker bound the harm. Requiring 'propose' to reach a follow-up word, or 'as ... request/job', would tighten it. The other phrases are whole-word and well tested (the_matcher_reads_whole_directive_phrases).

findings.summary: The CHANGELOG bullet is one very long paragraph.
findings.evidence: The single added bullet runs to about 400 words, covering root cause, mechanism, limits and test commands. It matches the neighbouring entries' style but is hard to scan.

summary: The change passes. When a job closes with a reading, each out_of_scope item that names separate work ('as its own job', 'as a follow-up request', 'propose … follow-up') is now queued as its own steward request citing the original job. The hook is one call in run/close.rs, close_dispatched, into a new followups.rs module. That module reuses the steward's request code (ProposedChange → RequestQueue::apply → StewardRequest::from_change/new), so there is no second request-text writer. I ran every planned demonstration and all tests passed: one request per follow-up item, plain exclusions and an empty list queue nothing, once-only behavior across a re-close, a failed job and its reworded retry, and a held job's resume, a cap of 5 per job, a path-less item falling back to records/, and the follow-ups showing in queued_work and the drain. Protected paths and Cargo files are unchanged. fmt, clippy and the full test suite were recorded passing by CI for this commit. There are no blockers or major issues. Minor points: the hook sits in close.rs rather than the listed manage.rs, though the plan named close.rs; the once-per-chain marker drops genuinely new follow-ups named by a later retry, a cost the CHANGELOG states; and 'propose' within three words of 'job' or 'request' can occasionally match a plain exclusion.
